sections.heading: Who should buy and who should skip
paragraphs: Buy a 2026 air fryer if you want faster crisp results with less oil for fries, wings, veggies, and frozen snacks — and you will leave it on the counter.
Skip oversized dual-basket or oven combos if you only reheat for one person; a 2–4 qt compact unit will be easier to store and clean.
bullets: Everyday family → 5–6 qt single basket (Cosori / Instant / Ninja)
Two foods at once → DualZone / dual basket

sections.heading: How to choose the right size in 2026
paragraphs: Match basket size to real meals: about 2–4 qt for individuals, 5–6 qt for most families, and 8+ qt or dual baskets when you batch wings or cook protein and sides together.
Dual baskets win when sync-finish matters. Oven-style air fryers win when you also toast and bake on a rack — but they need more counter depth.
bullets: 8+ qt or dual → batch cooking and two-zone meals

faqs.question: What is the best air fryer overall in 2026?
faqs.answer: For most homes, a 5–6 qt single-basket model like Cosori TurboBlaze or a strong Instant Vortex / Ninja Pro is the safest starting point. Choose DualZone if you regularly cook two foods that need to finish together.

faqs.question: What size air fryer do I need?
faqs.answer: Use about 2–4 qt for one to two people, 5–6 qt for most families, and 8+ qt or dual baskets for large batches or protein-plus-sides cooking.

faqs.question: Is a dual basket worth it in 2026?
faqs.answer: Yes if you often cook two foods with different settings. If you mostly make one tray of fries or wings, a single basket is simpler and usually cheaper.

faqs.question: Basket air fryer or toaster-oven air fryer?
faqs.answer: Basket models are usually faster and easier for everyday crisping. Oven-style units make more sense when you also want toast, bake, and rack capacity in one appliance.
